title: U.S. stock futures steady after Wall St retreats from records; yields climb
full_text:
Wall Street posts first red session of October a day after notching a record close
Investing.com-- U.S. stock futures were little changed on Wednesday evening after Wall Street retreated from record highs, as long-dated U.S. Treasury yields resumed their climb, reviving concerns about inflation, government debt and the outlook for interest rates.
S&P 500 Futures inched 0.1% lower to 7,847.25 points, while Nasdaq 100 Futures fell 0.1% to 31,383.75 points by 21:00 ET (01:00 GMT). Dow Jones Futures also traded 0.1% lower at 51,398.0 points.
The S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average and Nasdaq Composite all ended lower, with the S&P 500 and Dow snapping four-session winning streaks and the Nasdaq posting its first decline in six sessions.
The S&P 500 fell 0.2%, the Dow lost 0.7%, and the Nasdaq slipped 0.2%.
The retreat followed a renewed selloff in the Treasury market. The 10-year yield climbed as high as 5.36%, its highest level since 2002, while the 30-year yield briefly touched 5.70%, also a 24-year high.
Yields later pulled back after a well-received $39 billion auction of 10-year notes, easing some pressure on equities.
Investors digested minutes from the Federal Reserve’s September meeting, which showed policymakers broadly viewed the latest rate increase as a measure to contain persistent inflation rather than the start of an aggressive hiking cycle.
Markets have reduced expectations for an October rate increase. Traders were pricing in about an 18% probability of a hike at the Fed’s October meeting after the minutes were released, according to CME FedWatch.
Oil prices added to inflation concerns during the session. Brent crude remained above $100 a barrel as investors assessed supply disruptions linked to the Iran conflict and attacks by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabia.
Investors were also weighing corporate earnings and the strength of the global artificial-intelligence investment cycle.
Samsung Electronics (KS:005930) said on Thursday that its third-quarter operating profit was expected to jump nearly eightfold to a record 107.4 trillion won ($80.1 billion), helped by strong AI-driven demand for memory chips. The figure missed a Bloomberg forecast of 108.67 trillion won.
The Samsung results provided fresh evidence of strong demand for advanced memory used in AI infrastructure, benefiting chipmakers including Micron and SK Hynix. Samsung shares nevertheless fell in Seoul as investors focused on lofty expectations.
In the U.S., chip stocks had weakened during Wednesday’s session, with the semiconductor index falling 1.2%. SpaceX also declined after reports it was seeking $40 billion in financing to fund purchases of Nvidia chips.
Investors will now turn their attention to third-quarter earnings season. Strong corporate results could help support stocks, but elevated Treasury yields and oil prices remain key risks to the market’s record-setting rally.

title: Oil prices surge 2% on M.East shipping attacks, U.S. Gulf coast disruptions
full_text:
Wall Street posts first red session of October a day after notching a record close
Investing.com-- Oil prices rose sharply on Thursday following reports of more attacks on commercial shipping in the Middle East, while markets also braced for supply disruptions from adverse weather along the U.S. Gulf coast.
Crude largely rose past the International Energy Agency vowing to release more stockpiled oil, while other data showed an unexpected contraction in oil inventories.
Brent oil futures for December rose nearly 2% to $102.15 a barrel by 23:39 ET (03:39 GMT), while West Texas Intermediate crude futures for November rose 1.6% to $89.68 a barrel.
Get more insights on crude prices by subscribing to InvestingPro
Hormuz shipping attacks boost oil
Reports of increased Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz rattled oil markets, driving up expectations of more supply disruptions in the region.
The UK Maritime said on Wednesday evening that a tanker was struck by multiple projectiles just north of Qatar, with casualties reported from the incident.
Iranian attacks on tankers hit their highest level last week of any week since the U.S.-Iran war began, with Tehran reiterating that Hormuz remained close to commercial shipping.
The increased attacks came as shipping through Hormuz briefly hit pre-war levels in September.
Red Sea shipping and Saudi Arabia’s oil exports also remained a point of concern. Hostilities between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis continued to play out this week, with the Houthis seen attacking a refinery in Riyadh.
U.S. Gulf coast production in focus as Isaias approaches
Crude was also buoyed by mounting expectations of weather-related disruptions in the U.S. Gulf coast.
Tropical Storm Isaias is primed to rapidly strengthen into a dangerous hurricane and make landfall on the northern Gulf coast by the weekend, the U.S. National Weather Service said.
The storm is expected to bring intense rainfall and hurricane-force winds in the Gulf of Mexico. Several major oil and gas companies were seen evacuating non-essential personnel from their offshore facilities in the region.
The companies with the most exposure to production disruptions from the storm include BP, Chevron, and Shell.
A model cited by Reuters forecast up to 11.2 million barrels of oil production could be lost across the Gulf through the duration of the storm.
Separately, data released on Wednesday showed U.S. crude oil inventories fell by 3.2 million barrels in the week to October 2, ducking expectations for an increase.
Oil pared some gains on Wednesday after the IEA said completing the previously announced release of 400 million barrels of oil stocks as soon as possible would bring about 100 million barrels to the market.
But it was not immediately clear whether the move would entail an additional release of oil stockpiles.

title: Pentagon orders military to be ready for more Iran strikes, Axios reports
full_text:
Investing.com-- The Pentagon has instructed U.S. Central Command to complete preparations for a possible resumption of major combat operations in Iran, Axios reported late Wednesday, citing U.S. officials.
The directive did not set a date for potential strikes, and President Donald Trump has not made a final decision, Axios reported.
U.S. and Israeli officials said renewed military action could come before U.S. midterm elections, although the chances were considered low, with the likelihood rising significantly afterward, according to the report.
Any renewed campaign would likely involve extensive U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iranian energy, infrastructure and nuclear targets, Axios said.
Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spoke on Wednesday, their second call in several days, while Israel's security leadership also discussed Iran.
Negotiations mediated by Qatar have made little progress, with Tehran yet to respond to a U.S. counterproposal seeking nuclear concessions.

title: Amazon cuts fewer than 1,000 jobs across teams, Business Insider reports
full_text:
Wall Street posts first red session of October a day after notching a record close
Investing.com -- Amazon confirmed a new round of job cuts on Wednesday, primarily in its Stores division, adding to the company’s workforce reductions even as it ramps up spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure.
The latest cuts affect fewer than 1,000 white-collar employees across the U.S., India and the U.K., according to a person familiar with the matter cited by Business Insider, with employees reporting reductions across customer service, marketplace support and engineering roles within Amazon’s retail operations.
Amazon said the changes were intended to reshape parts of its Stores business around its current priorities, according to the report.
The cuts come after Amazon eliminated roughly 30,000 corporate jobs late last year and in January, as Chief Executive Andy Jassy sought to reduce layers of management, streamline the organization and lower costs.
The latest reductions have also created uncertainty among employees, with internal messages raising questions about severance, access to internal job openings and whether further notifications could follow.
Business Insider reported that some managers had scaled back planning for coming quarters because of expectations that teams or priorities could change.
Amazon said it was eliminating a small number of roles and would support affected employees during the transition, according to the report.
The restructuring is part of a wider shift across the technology sector, where companies are reducing jobs in some functions while directing more resources toward AI. Meta eliminated about 8,000 positions in May, while Microsoft cut more than 5,000 jobs between July and September.
Amazon has also been approaching some former employees, including people affected by previous layoffs, about openings in AWS and its AI businesses, highlighting the shift in where the company is directing talent and investment.
The latest cuts come during Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days promotional event, adding a notable timing element to the restructuring of its core retail operations.

title: Chinese stocks firm slightly as trade resumes after Golden Week break
full_text:
Wall Street posts first red session of October a day after notching a record close
Investing.com-- Chinese stocks firmed slightly on Thursday, resuming trade on a muted note after a week-long holiday as local markets digested fresh stimulus from Beijing and soaring global yields.
The Shanghai Shenzhen CSI 300 index rose 0.3% to 4,372.06 points in morning trade, while the Shanghai Composite rose 0.26% to 3,852.0 points.

Local markets reopened on a strong note tracking more stimulus and policy support from Beijing, after the government pledged to step up counter-cyclical policy support, and also vowed to stabilize the property market.
Additionally, the People’s Bank of China was seen cutting interest rates and injecting more liquidity into local markets since late-September.
Shipping stocks were among the best performers on Thursday, aided by soaring global freight rates due to disruptions stemming from the Middle East. Local banks and property stocks also advanced.
But Chinese markets struggled to hold gains amid a storm of headwinds, especially from soaring global bond yields. Technology stocks were hit hard by rising yields, which largely overshadowed optimism over artificial intelligence.
A rally in oil prices weighed, as markets braced for supply disruptions in the Middle East and looming disruptions in the U.S. Gulf coast.
Losses in Hong Kong markets, which were open during a part of the Golden Week break, also provided a weak lead-in for Chinese markets. The Hang Seng fell 0.45% on Thursday and was down 2.05% since late-September.
Locally, recent data showed Chinese consumers remained largely pessimistic, and that spending remained sluggish despite an extended Golden Week holiday.
But travel demand improved marginally during the break, although it was unclear whether this translated into firmer growth.
Focus now turns to the Communist Party’s fifth plenum, scheduled for October 26-29, for more cues on Beijing’s plans to shore up sluggish growth.

title: Gold holds near nine-week low as Hormuz tensions raise Fed hike bets
full_text:
Wall Street posts first red session of October a day after notching a record close
Investing.com -- Gold prices edged higher on Thursday after falling to their lowest level since early August, as renewed tensions around the Strait of Hormuz kept inflation risks elevated and reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates again this year.
At 21:36 ET (01:36 GMT), XAU/USD rose 0.6% to $4,134.19 an ounce, while Gold Futures gained 0.4% to $4,158.30. XAG/USD rose 1% to $60.37, while XPT/USD climbed 1.7% to $1,661.28. The U.S. Dollar Index was little changed at 102.23.
Hormuz tensions keep energy and inflation risks elevated
Tehran has stepped up attacks on tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz, adding to concerns over the security of a key global energy route.
The White House is also considering possible military strikes against Iranian targets ahead of the U.S. midterm elections in November.
While oil flows from the Middle East have recovered to near pre-conflict levels, the risks around the waterway have pushed shipping costs to record highs.
A tropical storm in the Gulf of Mexico was also putting further pressure on energy supplies, with MMA reporting that 25% of Gulf oil production had been shut.
The U.S.-Iran conflict has now run for more than seven months, and gold is down about 20% since the war erupted in late February.
Surging energy costs have fueled inflation and contributed to tighter monetary policy, weighing on gold as a non-yielding asset.
Fed minutes reinforce case for another hike
Fresh pressure on gold came from the Federal Reserve's latest meeting minutes. All 19 policymakers supported September's rate increase, while most believed another increase would be appropriate by year-end.
Markets are now pricing roughly a 20% probability of an October rate hike, but an 80% chance of a hike by December.
Higher Treasury yields and a stronger dollar have also weighed on investor demand for gold.
The greenback was trading near its strongest level of the year, making dollar-priced bullion more expensive for buyers using other currencies.
Still, central bank demand has provided an important cushion. ANZ analysts said in a note that strong buying by central banks helped limit gold's losses even as higher bond yields and a stronger U.S. dollar pressured investor demand.
The People's Bank of China increased its gold reserves by 740,000 ounces in September, marking its 23rd consecutive month of accumulation. China, one of the world's largest gold buyers, has also accelerated purchases in recent months following the decline in prices, according to ANZ.
That continued official-sector demand is helping offset some of the near-term pressure from higher yields, a stronger dollar and renewed energy-driven inflation concerns.

title: Asian currencies rangebound as dollar holds near 18-month high, yen slips
full_text:
Wall Street posts first red session of October a day after notching a record close
Investing.com -- Asian currencies remained largely rangebound on Thursday as the U.S. dollar held near an 18-month high, while the Japanese yen weakened as markets digested hawkish Federal Reserve minutes and fresh Japanese economic data.
The dollar's gains were limited by expectations that the Fed will pause its tightening cycle this month.
The U.S. dollar index was around 102.24, little changed, after rising 0.3% on Wednesday and remaining close to its strongest level since April 2025. The USD/JPY pair was around 158.15, up 0.05%, while the AUD/USD pair fell 0.1% to $0.6957, while the NZD/USD pair declined 0.2% to $0.5603.
Dollar holds near highs as Fed pause bets firm
The Federal Reserve's September meeting minutes showed policymakers continued to view inflation as the biggest risk to the U.S. outlook, although the discussion revealed divisions over the reasoning behind the quarter-point rate increase.
The minutes did little to alter expectations that the Fed will hold rates at its Oct. 28 meeting. CME FedWatch showed markets pricing a 19% probability of a 25-basis-point hike, unchanged from a day earlier.
DBS said the minutes reinforced expectations for an October pause followed by a possible December 9 hike.
The New York Fed also said one-year inflation expectations rose to a three-year high of 3.9% in September.
DBS noted that although WTI has not returned to its April peak, gasoline prices have moved back toward their 2026 high and diesel has reached new highs amid tight distillate supplies.
That could undermine the argument that U.S. energy production shields the economy from global fuel-price shocks, potentially limiting some of the dollar's support from higher rates.
Yen weakens as Japan data, BOJ outlook in focus
The USD/JPY pair remained around 158.15 after rising as high as 158.22.
Japan's current-account surplus reached ¥4.062 trillion in August, above the ¥3.19 trillion median forecast, providing a stronger external-balance backdrop for the yen.
The currency nevertheless remained weak after the latest BOJ signals suggested policymakers remain divided on the timing of further increases.
Markets continue to assess the prospect of additional tightening against concerns over fiscal spending and the impact of higher yields.
The yen is also sensitive to intervention risks after Japanese officials repeatedly warned against excessive weakness.
Rupee pressured after RBI turns hawkish
The USD/INR pair rose 0.2% to 96.987, leaving the rupee close to its recent record low despite the Reserve Bank of India's shift toward tighter policy.
The RBI raised its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% at its latest meeting and adopted a more hawkish stance, with Governor Sanjay Malhotra signaling that further action would depend on inflation and economic conditions.
The rupee has nevertheless remained vulnerable to the stronger dollar, elevated U.S. yields and oil prices above $100 a barrel.
The rate decision is now likely to provide a domestic support for the currency, but external drivers remain the larger influence on the pair.
China's financial markets returned on Thursday after the week-long National Day holiday, bringing the onshore yuan back into focus.
The USD/CNH pair rose marginally to 6.704, while the USD/CNY pair fell slightly to 6.703. The USD/KRW pair fell 0.1% to 1,337.43 and the USD/SGD pair was little changed.

title: Hormuz transits at lowest in over two months after attacks, data shows
full_text:
Wall Street posts first red session of October a day after notching a record close
By Florence Tan
SINGAPORE, Oct 8 (Reuters) - The number of vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz fell to the lowest in more than two months after attacks on tankers in the key waterway reached their highest last week since the start of the US-Israeli war with Iran, shipping data showed.
Seven commodity vessels passed through the strait on Tuesday, for the lowest figure since July 23, data from analytics firm Kpler showed.
"Crude crossing the strait fell 27% from a wartime high the week before, to at least 10.1 million barrels a day," Kpler analysts Emmanuel Belostrino and Yui Torikata wrote in a note on October 6.
"That is back to its September average, but 74% of its pre-war level."
Most of the fall was in ship-to-ship (STS) transfers in the Gulf of Oman, where cargoes move between tankers, they added.
However, exports from the Gulf of Oman coast and the Red Sea rose to 6.7 million bpd, more than twice pre-war levels, analysts said, making up for lost supply from Hormuz.
This helped keep overall exports of Middle East crude at the pre-war level, they said.
The number of vessels transiting the strait edged up to 10 on Wednesday, but was well short of the daily tally of more than 20 on Sunday and Monday, the data showed.
More vessels entered the strait than exited in the past two days.
The figures exclude vessels crossing with their Automatic Identification System transponders turned off to avoid detection.
LSEG data of all vessels crossing the strait showed eight on Tuesday, evenly divided between entries and exits, down from the previous day’s 14.
These included five oil tankers and the liquefied natural gas tanker Al Mafyar which loaded at Ras Laffan in Qatar and was set to head for Port Qasim in Pakistan, LSEG added.
Attacks on tankers sailing through Hormuz hit their highest last week of any week since the Iran war began, maritime security sources tracking incidents said, as Gulf producers made a bigger export push.
In the latest incident, projectiles struck a tanker 51 nautical miles north of Qatar’s Madinat ash Shamal, with casualties reported, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said on Wednesday.
Before the February 28 start of the Iran war, about 125 large commercial vessels went through the strait each per day, comprising tankers, gas carriers, bulkers and container vessels.
Their cargoes accounted for a fifth of global supplies of crude oil and liquefied natural gas.

title: Qualcomm and Arm kick off trial, potential for huge damages in focus
full_text:
Wall Street posts first red session of October a day after notching a record close
(Corrects paragraph 10 to reflect that Arm was seeking an 18,500% increase in royalty rates, not 1,800%)
By Tom Hals, Max A. Cherney and Stephen Nellis
WILMINGTON, Delaware, Oct 5 (Reuters) - Chipmaker Qualcomm and chip tech firm Arm Holdings, long at loggerheads, began another trial on Monday, with Qualcomm accusing Arm of withholding chip testing tools that were due under contract.
Qualcomm also alleges that Arm leaked to the media its 2024 threat to terminate a vital license agreement in a way that damaged discussions for a chip deal between Qualcomm and Meta Platforms.
In the lawsuit brought before US federal court in Delaware, Qualcomm, one of Arm’s largest customers, is seeking to quit paying royalties — potentially worth billions of dollars — to Arm for up to five years.
Qualcomm attorney Karen Dunn said in her opening statement that Qualcomm had been on the cusp of a deal with Meta when Arm notified Qualcomm that it was in breach of its architecture agreement and then allegedly leaked that notification letter to Bloomberg News.
Meta became concerned Qualcomm would lose its license and Dunn told the jury that by the time Qualcomm secured the Meta deal the value had decreased by $170 million. “Delay is costly,” she told the jury.
But Arm’s attorney Gregg LoCascio told the jury it would learn that what really happened is Meta shifted to AI eyeglasses and away from virtual reality headsets and sought to adjust financial terms for Qualcomm chips as a result.
“They were not harmed in the least,” LoCascio said.
While a five-year hold on royalty payments sought by Qualcomm could be a major sales impact for Arm, Judge Maryellen Noreika is weighing whether to throw out that term of the contract, which could mean Qualcomm would be able to seek only a smaller amount of damages.
In a related bench trial, Noreika also heard arguments over whether Arm has negotiated in good faith with Qualcomm for the next version of Arm’s chip technology. Qualcomm’s agreement with Arm runs through 2033.
Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon testified during the bench trial portion of Monday’s proceedings, during which Qualcomm’s attorney returned repeatedly to a chart that showed Arm was seeking an increase of 18,500% in its royalty payments between version 9 and version 10 of its computing architecture.
During a cross-examination, Arm’s attorney pressed Amon on whether Qualcomm was aiming to get Arm to stick to pricing in a 2013 architecture licensing deal that capped royalties at $1.88 per chip for any chip with at least five central processor cores.
Arm’s attorney asked Amon whether that agreement, which dates from an era of smaller smartphone chips, was under-priced in 2026’s market, where some data center chips have 288 central processor cores. The attorney asked Amon if the deal structure means that Qualcomm would be paying royalties for five central processor cores on larger chips and “getting 283 for free.”
Amon responded that “I don’t see it that way.”
The five-day trial marks another stage in the contentious relationship between Arm and Qualcomm.
Arm sued Qualcomm in 2022 alleging that Qualcomm had breached its contracts, though Qualcomm came away in 2024 with a key victory.

title: European shares drift to 4-month lows on mega-debt swaps, and French debt woes
full_text:
Wall Street posts first red session of October a day after notching a record close
Investing.com - European stocks skid to their lowest level in nearly four months, as desks wrestled with a toxic cocktail of surging corporate bond supply in the U.S., persistent Middle East energy shocks, and a hawkish monetary signal from the Federal Reserve.
The pan-European Stoxx Europe 600 Index dropped 1% to its lowest level since June 11, after snapping a three-session winning streak on Wednesday.
Germany’s DAX fell 1% while, France’s CAC 40 slid 0.9%. London’s FTSE 100 was down 0.7% Italy’s FTSE MIB fell the most, down 1.3%.
While European equities mounted a fragile mid-week rally to claw back ground from three-month lows, broader risk appetite remains severely constrained by a global fixed-income sell-off and widening fiscal fissures across continental bourses.
US tech mega-debt spree squeezes blobal fixed-income bourses
A fresh source of friction hit international bond markets overnight as reports surfaced that major U.S. technology titans - including SpaceX and Broadcom - are preparing to raise a staggering $80 billion in mega-debt issuances.
The prospective mega-issuance spree has sparked fears of direct competition for institutional capital, crowding out sovereign paper and driving corporate credit spreads wider.
While European bourses carry less direct exposure to pure-play AI tech mega-caps, continental shares faced indirect headwinds as major European industrial and tech firms serve as primary suppliers and clients to those American giants.
Tech stocks such as Infineon fell 2.7%, while ASML holdings fell 2.3%. BE Semiconductor and STMicroelectronics dropped 2.6% each.
Persian Gulf strikes re-ignite oil and gas curves
Adding to the stagflationary headwinds, crude oil and European wholesale natural gas futures spiked as military hostilities across Middle Eastern maritime choke points intensified.
A fresh surge in drone and missile attacks targeting commercial shipping and energy infrastructure in the Persian Gulf and Red Sea reignited geopolitical risk premia.
The escalation effectively erased recent price declines, forcing energy-intensive European sectors to price in elevated winter fuel costs just as space-heating demand begins across Northwestern Europe.
Hawkish Fed minutes and Bank of France warning anchor CAC 40
Macroeconomic sentiment across continental desks was further chilled by Wednesday’s release of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) September meeting minutes. The readout revealed that a majority of Fed policymakers still considered another interest rate hike likely before year-end, dashing hopes for a swift transition to monetary easing.
Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin acknowledged on Wednesday that the nation’s fiscal and economic situation was "serious," driven by widening budget deficits and political uncertainty.
However, Moulin firmly dismissed calls for central bank intervention, stating that Paris does not require assistance from the European Central Bank and must address its structural deficit through domestic budget reform.
Underperforming its continental peers, France’s CAC 40 lingered at its lowest levels since March. The French benchmark remains on track for its second consecutive weekly decline as investors demand an elevated risk premium to hold French equities and sovereign paper ahead of protracted budget negotiations.
French banks faced sharp sell-offs because they hold massive inventories of domestic government bonds. Societe Generale and BNP Paribas fell over 2% each.

title: TSMC Q3 sales beat estimates on surging AI chip demand
full_text:
Wall Street posts first red session of October a day after notching a record close
Investing.com-- Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co’s (TW:2330) third-quarter revenue topped market expectations as surging demand for artificial intelligence chips continued to fuel growth at the world’s largest contract chipmaker.
Third-quarter revenue reached about NT$1.49 trillion ($46.7 billion), according to calculations, up 50% from a year earlier and exceeding the NT$1.46 trillion estimate from analysts surveyed by Bloomberg.
September revenue jumped 55% year on year to NT$511.86 billion, TSMC said on Thursday. The figure was down 0.6% from August.
Taipei-listed shares of the company fell more than 1% to NT$2,555.0 by 05:45 GMT.
The results underscore continued strength in demand for advanced chips used in AI accelerators and data centers, benefiting TSMC customers including Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) and Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL).

title: Musk accuses ’certain oligarchs’ of blocking Starlink launch in India
full_text:
Wall Street posts first red session of October a day after notching a record close
Updates with India communications ministry statement
Investing.com-- Elon Musk said on Wednesday that unnamed rivals were preventing SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) from launching its Starlink satellite broadband service in India, in an apparent reference to billionaires Mukesh Ambani and Sunil Bharti Mittal.
"Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people," Musk wrote in a post on X. "You can guess who they are …"
SpaceX has been waiting for approval from Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government to begin offering Starlink services in India, a move that could see it eventually compete with companies controlled by Ambani’s Reliance Industries and Mittal’s Bharti Airtel, which have established strong positions in the country’s telecommunications sector.
Get more breaking news on Musk and SpaceX by subscribing to InvestingPro
India’s communications ministry said in a statement on Thursday that the country’s regulatory framework for satellite communication services was "fair and non-discriminatory."
The ministry added that it had granted telecom licenses to three satellite communication operators, and that every such licensee was required to comply with Indian security requirements.
Earlier reporting showed Airtel-backed Eutelsat OneWeb, Jio Satellite Communications, and Starlink were granted licenses by India. Starlink was the latest licensee, having received the permit in June.
But beyond the telecom licenses, the three still need spectrum assignment and a final clearance from the Indian government to begin providing services.
"At present, all the three entities are at broadly the same regulatory stage," India’s telecom ministry said.
Reliance Jio Infocomm and Bharti Airtel, India’s two largest private telecommunications operators, serve approximately 910 million broadband subscribers combined. This represents more than 80% of the country’s market, according to the latest government data.
India had effectively stopped final approvals for Starlink’s commercial launch due to security concerns. In June, reports showed that security agencies under the country’s home ministry withheld clearances for the low-Earth orbit service to begin operations.

title: Imperial Brands shares hit near two-month high after £1.5 billion buyback launch
full_text:

Investing.com -- Imperial Brands PLC (LON:IMB) said on Thursday it remains on track to deliver its full-year FY26 targets across all key metrics, supported by continued tobacco revenue growth and strong momentum in next-generation products, while announcing a further £1.5 billion share buyback.
The tobacco maker expects low-single-digit tobacco net revenue growth, double-digit NGP net revenue growth and group adjusted operating profit growth within its 3%-5% guidance range. It also expects high-single-digit adjusted EPS growth and more than £2.2 billion of free cash flow for the year.

Imperial said adjusted operating-profit growth should remain within its 3%-5% target range, while adjusted earnings per share are expected to increase at a high-single-digit rate.
The company said it is now launching a further £1.5 billion buyback for FY27, which it expects to complete no later than October 29, 2027.
Imperial said it has returned almost £13 billion to shareholders through dividends and buybacks between FY21 and FY26, while reducing its issued share capital by more than 21% since the buyback programme began in October 2022.
The company remains confident of delivering at least £320 million in savings by 2030, including manufacturing initiatives that underpin a targeted £100 million reduction in overheads.

title: Argenx shares plunge 16% after Sjögren’s drug trial halted
full_text:
Wall Street posts first red session of October a day after notching a record close
Investing.com -- Shares in Belgian biotech argenx tumbled over 16% on Thursday after it said it would stop a late-stage trial of its drug efgartigimod in Sjögren’s disease because an interim analysis showed it was unlikely to succeed.
An independent data monitoring committee recommended stopping the Phase 3 UNITY study after the interim analysis concluded the trial would be unable to meet its primary endpoint, the company said. Safety results were consistent with the drug’s established profile, and no new safety signals were identified.
The study tested efgartigimod, given as an injection under the skin, in adults with moderate-to-severe Sjögren’s disease. Patients were randomly assigned to receive weekly efgartigimod or a placebo in a double-blind trial.
The main goal was to measure the change from baseline in overall disease activity at Week 48, using the clinical EULAR Sjögren’s Syndrome Disease Activity Index.
"We are disappointed by this outcome, most of all for people living with Sjögren’s disease, who are still waiting for treatments that fundamentally change the course of their disease," said Luc Truyen, Chief Medical Officer at argenx in a statement.
The company said it will carry out a full analysis of the data after the study closes and the database is locked, to understand the outcome and draw lessons for future research in Sjögren’s disease.
Sjögren’s disease is a long-term inflammatory autoimmune disease in which the immune system destroys the body’s exocrine glands. It mainly affects women, with a 9:1 female-to-male ratio.
Efgartigimod is approved for generalized myasthenia gravis and immune thrombocytopenia in Japan. The injected version is approved for generalized myasthenia gravis and chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy.
